sentences.text: Fasolasuchus is an extinct genus of loricatan, a group of large, armored reptiles.
Scientists estimate this animal reached a length of 8 to 10 meters and weighed approximately 1.6 tons.
Its back featured two distinct rows of osteoderms, which are bony plates embedded in the skin.
Unlike most rauisuchians, which typically have two rows on their tails, Fasolasuchus possessed only a single row on its tail.
The skeleton included a hyposphene-hypantrum articulation, a joint structure that added extra rigidity to the vertebral column.
In the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — the femur measures 70 cm in length, which is double the length of the fibula.
Fasolasuchus is considered the largest known non-dinosaurian terrestrial predator.
Fossils were discovered in the Los Colorados Formation in northwestern Argentina.
The genus name Fasolasuchus honors Tomás H. Fasola, who found the specimen and collaborated on Bonaparte's expeditions to the Triassic of Argentina.
The known specimen was somatically and skeletally mature, but its sexual maturity could not be determined.
A 2011 study by Nesbitt provided a cladogram placing Fasolasuchus within its evolutionary context.
Fasolasuchus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, existing between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
Additional fossils found in Argentina date to the Rhaetian stage of the Late Triassic.
